title: Methods
text:
The TCGA exploration uses a standardized pan-cancer framework to evaluate candidate kinase expression across the 33 TCGA cancer projects.
Analyses are performed only where the required molecular and clinical data are available.

title: Methods
text:
The TCGA exploration uses a standardized pan-cancer framework to evaluate candidate kinase expression across the 33 TCGA cancer projects.
Analyses are performed only where the required molecular and clinical data are available.

title: Methods
text:
Expression data
Harmonized TCGA STAR gene-count files were used.
Expression analyses use the tpm_unstranded field.
For JAK3, expression was extracted across all available TCGA projects and linked with sample-level and clinical metadata.

title: Methods
text:
Patient-level handling
Where more than one expression aliquot represented the same patient and sample type, expression was collapsed to patient level using the standardized pan-cancer workflow.

title: Methods
text:
Tumor versus normal
Primary malignant samples were compared with Solid Tissue Normal samples where both groups were available.
The canonical tumor-normal analysis used the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.
Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied across the tested cancer types.

title: Methods
text:
Matched tumor-normal
Where a patient had both tumor and normal samples, a paired tumor-normal analysis was performed.
The paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used.

title: Methods
text:
Early-stage tumor versus normal
Early-stage tumors were defined using AJCC Stage I classifications, including Stage IA, IB and IC where applicable.
Stage-I tumors were compared with Solid Tissue Normal samples.

title: Methods
text:
Stage-wise analysis
Stage analyses were performed only where sufficiently populated stage groups were available.
Two complementary tests were retained:

categorical differences across stage groups
monotonic stage-expression trends

Kruskal-Wallis testing was used for categorical stage differences.
Spearman correlation was used to evaluate monotonic stage trends.

title: Methods
text:
Grade-wise analysis
Grade analyses were performed only where grade labels could be standardized into interpretable ordered groups with sufficient sample sizes.
Categorical grade differences and monotonic grade-expression trends were both assessed.

title: Methods
text:
High or aberrant expression
Where normal tissue was available, the 95th percentile of the normal-tissue TPM distribution was used as the reference threshold.
Tumors above this threshold were counted as showing high or aberrant expression relative to the corresponding normal-tissue distribution.

title: Methods
text:
Survival analysis
Survival was treated as secondary evidence.
Curated TCGA Clinical Data Resource endpoints were used.
Continuous log2(TPM + 1) expression was evaluated using Cox proportional-hazards models.
The following information was retained:

sample size
number of events
hazard ratio
95% confidence interval
false-discovery-rate-adjusted significance
proportional-hazards diagnostic
low-event-count flag

title: Methods
text:
Immune and inflammatory infiltration controls
TCGA RNA-seq represents bulk tissue, so observed expression may reflect both malignant-cell biology and differences in immune or stromal cell content.
Several complementary controls were therefore used.

Leukocyte fraction
PanImmune leukocyte-fraction estimates were matched to TCGA tumors.
JAK3 expression was evaluated against leukocyte fraction using correlation and regression analyses.
Stage and grade analyses were also repeated with measured leukocyte fraction included as a covariate where possible.


CIBERSORT
CIBERSORT relative immune-cell fractions were evaluated for 22 immune cell types.
The analysis included:

primary quality-filtered correlations
all-sample sensitivity analysis
leukocyte-fraction-adjusted cell-composition models
robustness checks across these analytical layers

Because CIBERSORT relative fractions are compositional, cell types were not entered simultaneously into one 22-variable regression model.


Immune marker correlations
Expression-based immune controls used the following markers:
PTPRC, CD3D, CD3E, MS4A1, CD79A, NKG7, LST1, TYROBP, FCER1G, CD68
Marker expression was transformed using log2(TPM + 1).


Multi-marker immune score
Within each cancer cohort, the ten log-transformed immune markers were standardized separately.
The immune score was calculated as the equal-weighted mean of the standardized marker values.
JAK3 itself was not included in this score.


Immune-adjusted tumor-normal models
Three prespecified linear models were evaluated for both:

all primary tumors versus normal tissue
Stage-I tumors versus normal tissue

The models were:

unadjusted group association
group association adjusted for PTPRC/CD45
group association adjusted for the multi-marker immune score

Persistence after immune adjustment was evaluated within this same linear-model family.

title: Methods
text:
Multiple testing
Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was used for prespecified analysis families.
Both analysis-specific and broader pan-cancer adjusted results were retained where appropriate.

title: Methods
text:
Sample sizes and limitations
Each analysis retains the relevant sample sizes and low-sample-size flags.
Not every analytical module can be performed for every TCGA cancer project because availability varies for:

normal tissue
matched tumor-normal samples
Stage-I tumors
stage annotation
grade annotation
survival events
immune-infiltration estimates

title: Methods
text:
Interpretation
This analysis is an observational bulk-RNA pan-cancer screen.
A significant immune-adjusted association means that the expression association remains after adjustment for the measured immune proxy.
It does not prove that expression originates from malignant cells.
Similarly, expression elevation in Stage-I tumors is compatible with an early-disease association but does not establish a causal role in tumor initiation.

title: Methods
text:
Reproducibility
Canonical final result tables and the final analysis pipeline are retained in the repository.
Raw TCGA STAR files are not stored in version control.

title: Methods
text:
Multikinase extension
The completed JAK3 framework was extended to the candidate panel:
JAK3, MET, HCK, LYN, DDR1, IRAK2, FJX1, EPHB1, RPS6KA2, EPHB2
JAK3 was retained as the completed reference benchmark.
The same patient-level RNA, tumor-normal, early-stage, progression, survival and immune-adjusted framework was applied across the panel.

title: Methods
text:
TCGA ATAC regulatory analysis
Official peak-to-gene regulatory links were obtained from the TCGA pan-cancer ATAC Data S7 dataset.
Across the candidate panel, 51 official linked regulatory elements were identified.
Some linked elements represented a single fixed-width ATAC peak, whereas broader enhancer units contained multiple constituent peaks.
For broader units, the official Summits field was parsed and each summit was mapped to the normalized TCGA ATAC matrix peak containing that summit.
All 74 constituent summits mapped successfully, retaining all 51 official regulatory elements.
For regulatory units containing multiple constituent peaks, accessibility was summarized using the mean of the constituent log2-normalized ATAC values.
Technical replicates belonging to the same tissue fragment were collapsed before patient-level analysis.

title: Methods
text:
Patient-matched ATAC-RNA analysis
Primary malignant RNA expression was summarized at patient level by averaging TPM across eligible aliquots followed by transformation as:
log2(TPM + 1)
ATAC accessibility and RNA expression were matched by gene, cancer type, patient and linked regulatory element.
Spearman correlation was calculated separately for each gene-cancer-regulatory-element combination.
Analyses were classified according to matched sample size:

at least 10 patients: primary analysis
5-9 patients: exploratory low-sample-size analysis
fewer than 5 patients: not tested

Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment was applied to primary analyses.
A gene-specific global FDR was calculated across eligible tests for each gene, and a second multikinase-wide FDR was calculated across all eligible primary tests.
Direction concordance with the official Data S7 regulatory correlation was also retained.

title: Methods
text:
Final multi-omic integration
Six normalized evidence domains were integrated:

primary tumor RNA
early-stage RNA
stage/grade progression
survival
immune-adjusted progression
ATAC-RNA regulatory coupling

The final multi-omic evidence index is the mean support across these six domains.
The ATAC component was normalized by eligible-test significance and cancer-level coverage so that genes with larger numbers of linked regulatory elements were not automatically favored.
The integrated index and JAK3 benchmark-domain counts are descriptive prioritization tools. They are not probabilities, causal estimates or formal statistical rankings.
The original innate-memory classification is retained separately from the TCGA validation score.

title: JAK3
text:
JAK3 tumor prioritization
To facilitate rapid identification of tumor types with the most compelling JAK3 signal, an integrated descriptive ranking was generated using three equally weighted criteria:

strength of significant tumor-versus-normal upregulation,
strength of significant Stage-I-versus-normal upregulation, and
persistence of the positive association after immune-content adjustment.

Immune robustness was assessed using both PTPRC/CD45 and the 10-marker ImmuneScore in the tumor-normal and Stage-I comparisons. The priority score is a descriptive prioritization metric rather than an additional statistical test.

The linked elements included JAK3_m1 approximately 2.6 kb from the JAK3 transcription start site, JAK3_p1 approximately 241.6 kb away, and the promoter-proximal JAK3_p2 element approximately 0.36 kb from the transcription start site.






Figure 2: JAK3 RNA prioritization and accessibility of the three official TCGA JAK3-linked ATAC elements. Values within the ATAC columns are median normalized accessibility values.



The chromatin-accessibility pattern was not identical to the RNA-based tumor ranking. HNSC showed comparatively high accessibility across all three linked elements, while CHOL and KIRC also showed substantial accessibility at the promoter-proximal JAK3_p2 element.


Patient-matched ATAC-RNA associations
ATAC samples were matched to the canonical TCGA JAK3 RNA-seq dataset using TCGA patient identifiers. Of 176 unique patients represented in the nine prioritized ATAC cohorts, 171 had matched primary-tumor JAK3 RNA measurements.
Within each cancer, accessibility of the three JAK3-linked elements was correlated with JAK3 expression using Spearman correlation. Tests with at least 10 matched patients were considered primary analyses. Tests with 5-9 patients were treated as exploratory, while groups with fewer than 5 matched patients were not tested inferentially. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied globally across the 21 primary cancer-element tests.
Across the 21 primary tests, 19 associations were positive and eight remained significant after global FDR correction. The promoter-proximal JAK3_p2 element showed significant positive associations with JAK3 expression in KIRC, KIRP, THCA, LUAD, COAD and LIHC. JAK3_m1 was also significant in LUAD and COAD.






Figure 3: Patient-matched within-cancer correlations between accessibility of official JAK3-linked ATAC elements and JAK3 RNA expression. Asterisks indicate global BH-FDR below 0.05 for primary analyses with at least 10 matched patients; daggers indicate exploratory analyses with 5-9 matched patients.



These results provide chromatin-level support for coordinated JAK3 accessibility and expression in several prioritized tumor types. They do not establish that chromatin accessibility causes JAK3 upregulation or that the observed signal is malignant-cell intrinsic, because the TCGA measurements represent bulk tumor tissue.

The multikinase module uses JAK3 as the completed benchmark and extends the framework to nine additional candidates emerging from the innate immune-memory analysis.

title: TCGA Pan-Cancer Kinase Exploration
text:
Interpretation
TCGA RNA-seq represents bulk tissue. Observed kinase expression may therefore reflect both malignant-cell biology and differences in immune or stromal cell content.
Associations that remain after adjustment for measured immune proxies are described as immune-adjusted or residual associations. They should not be interpreted as proof of malignant-cell-intrinsic expression.
Early-stage elevation is considered evidence of an association with early disease and does not establish a causal role in tumor initiation.

title: Multikinase Analysis
text:
TCGA ATAC regulatory analysis
Official TCGA pan-cancer ATAC Data S7 peak-to-gene links were used.
Across the ten genes, 51 official linked regulatory elements were identified.
Some elements represented single fixed-width ATAC peaks, while broader enhancer units contained multiple constituent peaks.
The official Summits field was therefore used to map the regulatory units to the normalized TCGA ATAC matrix.
All 74 constituent summits mapped successfully, preserving all 51 official regulatory elements.
JAK3 retained its original simple structure of three linked regulatory elements corresponding to three individual ATAC peaks.

title: Multikinase Analysis
text:
Patient-matched ATAC-RNA analysis
ATAC accessibility was matched to RNA expression from the same TCGA patients.
RNA expression was summarized at patient level using mean TPM followed by log2(TPM + 1) transformation.
Spearman correlations were calculated independently for each gene-cancer-regulatory-element combination.
Analyses were classified as:

Primary: at least 10 matched patients
Exploratory low N: 5-9 matched patients
Not tested: fewer than 5 matched patients

Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied to primary tests.
The expanded analysis reproduced the previously completed JAK3 ATAC-RNA pattern, providing an internal validation of the multikinase workflow.

title: Multikinase Analysis
text:
Cancer-specific ATAC-RNA coupling



Cancer-specific significant patient-matched ATAC-RNA associations. Color represents the strongest significant Spearman correlation and numbers indicate the number of significant linked elements. Blank cells indicate no FDR-significant association.


Most significant associations were positive and directionally concordant with the official Data S7 regulatory links.
A positive association means that higher accessibility at the linked element is associated with higher expression of the linked gene within that cancer cohort. It does not establish causal regulation.

title: Multikinase Analysis
text:
RNA versus ATAC evidence landscape



Integrated RNA evidence versus normalized ATAC-RNA evidence. Dashed lines indicate the JAK3 reference values.


This comparison separates several important patterns:

EPHB2 has the strongest integrated RNA evidence.
LYN has the strongest normalized ATAC-RNA support.
HCK lies close to JAK3 across both dimensions.
IRAK2 shows balanced support.
FJX1 has relatively strong RNA evidence but very limited normalized ATAC-RNA support.

title: Multikinase Analysis
text:
Primary follow-up candidates

EPHB2
EPHB2 is washout-emergent, rather than strict persistent, in the original macrophage analysis. It nevertheless shows the strongest overall integrated TCGA evidence, including early-stage, progression, survival and broad regulatory support.


HCK
HCK is a strict persistent candidate with one of the most balanced multi-domain profiles relative to JAK3.


LYN
LYN is a strict persistent candidate with particularly strong normalized ATAC-RNA support across multiple cancer types.


IRAK2
IRAK2 is a strict persistent candidate with balanced RNA, immune-adjusted and chromatin evidence.

title: Multikinase Analysis
text:
Secondary and contextual candidates
DDR1 remains a secondary candidate because its individual ATAC-RNA associations can be strong but are less broadly distributed.
RPS6KA2 shows substantial regulatory evidence but weaker overall RNA and clinical support.
MET retains substantial TCGA RNA and ATAC-RNA associations, but its original macrophage chromatin evidence did not survive corrected normalization and it remains RNA-only at the discovery chromatin layer.
EPHB1 has several regulatory associations but weaker integrated RNA and clinical support.
FJX1 has strong RNA-level evidence but limited normalized ATAC-RNA support. Its kinase-family classification should be confirmed before kinase-level mechanistic interpretation.

title: Multikinase Analysis
text:
Conclusion
The strongest follow-up group is EPHB2, HCK, LYN and IRAK2.
Their strengths arise from different evidence domains, supporting candidate-specific mechanistic follow-up rather than a single linear ranking.
The completed JAK3 analysis remains the reference module.
Detailed analytical definitions are provided on the Methods page.
